html:
A war fought around 595 to 585 BCE by a league of Greek states, the Amphictyonic League, against the town of Kirrha, which controlled the road from the sea up to the Oracle of Delphi.

Kirrha was accused of charging pilgrims and of disrespect to the sanctuary. The allies included Thessaly, Athens and Cleisthenes, tyrant of Sicyon. Later stories say the besiegers poisoned Kirrha's water supply, and some credit the idea to Solon. Kirrha was destroyed and its plain dedicated to Apollo, never to be farmed.

The win put Delphi under the protection of the league rather than any one city. The Pythian Games were then refounded with athletic contests, held every four years like the Olympic Games. Later "sacred wars" over Delphi, such as the Third Sacred War, let Philip II of Macedon into Greek affairs.
sum: A war fought around 595 to 585 BCE by a league of Greek states, the Amphictyonic League, against the town of Kirrha, which controlled the road from the sea up to the Oracle of Delphi.
